title: Indrajit's death
hook: an uncle and a nephew face each other at the fire, and Lakshmana makes a vow on his brother's name

segments.voice: Yesterday: Indrajit's cruelest trick, a magic Sita cut down to stop the army, and Vibhishana saying look again. It isn't what it seems.

The grove at Nikumbhila is dark with trees, and somewhere inside, a fire is burning. Lakshmana's army crashes into the rakshasas guarding it, and the fighting gets so loud and close that Indrajit has to leave his offering unfinished and come out. He climbs into his chariot. And the first face he sees in the enemy line isn't Lakshmana's. It's his uncle's: Vibhishana, who knew about the fire, the grove and the secret condition, and brought them here.
screen: `THE FIRE IN THE GROVE.` → `THE RITE LEFT UNFINISHED.` → `HIS UNCLE'S FACE.`

segments.voice: Indrajit's words are bitter. You were born here, he says, you're my father's brother, and you've brought the enemy to your own nephew. You've thrown away your family and your people to serve strangers. Vibhishana answers without shouting. I was born among the rakshasas, he says, but my nature isn't cruel. I left my brother because of what he was doing: carrying off another man's wife, harming those who had done him no wrong. I couldn't take part in it. Both of them speak from loyalty; they just mean different things by it. Then the duel begins, Lakshmana and Indrajit, long and close: chariots wrecked, armor split, both men bleeding, neither giving way. At last Lakshmana fits to his bow the weapon of Indra, king of the gods, and before he lets it go, he speaks a vow. If Rama, son of Dasharatha, is righteous, true to his word and unmatched in courage, then let this arrow kill Ravana's son. The arrow flies, and Indrajit falls. Lakshmana doesn't rest the arrow on his own strength. He rests it on his brother's goodness. And the warrior named conqueror of Indra is brought down, at last, by Indra's own weapon. In Lanka, Ravana hears and loses his mind with grief. He grabs his sword and rushes toward the ashoka grove to kill Sita. A minister named Suparshva steps in front of him. You, a learned king, would kill a woman? Fight Rama instead. Ravana turns back.
screen: `YOU BETRAYED YOUR FAMILY.` · `MY NATURE ISN'T CRUEL.` · `A VOW ON RAMA'S GOODNESS.` · `SUPARSHVA STOPS THE SWORD.` · then, large: `BROUGHT DOWN BY INDRA'S OWN WEAPON.`

segments.voice: Let one person whose goodness you trust completely come to mind: a parent, a teacher, a friend. For a few slow breaths, let whatever you're facing rest on their steadiness, the way Lakshmana rested his arrow on Rama's goodness.
Indrajit's death. At Nikumbhila, his rite broken, he falls to Lakshmana's arrow of Indra, shot on a vow resting on Rama's goodness.
Your line: a vow on Rama's goodness. With his son gone, Ravana has no one left to send. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Lakshmana's vow before the final arrow, resting on Rama's righteousness and truth, is often quoted by Ramayana teachers as a picture of Lakshmana's devotion to his brother.

original.note: Sanskrit aindrāstra: the weapon of Indra, from aindra, belonging to Indra, and astra, weapon.

trapdoor: what you thought: Lakshmana simply outfought Indrajit.
what it means: he shot Indra's weapon on a vow resting on Rama's righteousness.
what a scholar hears: the name Indrajit means conqueror of Indra, and the arrow that ends him is Indra's own weapon.

chat.says: What did Lakshmana say right before the arrow that killed Indrajit?
options: He vowed: if Rama is righteous and true, let this arrow kill Ravana's son.
He prayed for enough strength to win the duel by his own power alone.
He asked Indrajit one last time to surrender and join Rama's side.
chat.meaning: Lakshmana rests his final arrow not on his own strength but on his brother's goodness, and Indra's weapon brings down Indra's conqueror.

Nikumbhila.meaning: the sacred grove where Indrajit's fire rite is broken

Dasharatha.meaning: Rama's father, the king of Ayodhya

Suparshva.meaning: a minister who stops Ravana from killing Sita

Indra.meaning: king of the gods, whose weapon Lakshmana uses

recall: the young king, the heir who shares rule

notes: Sarga numbers follow the common (vulgate) numbering; confirm.
Vibhishana's reply to Indrajit is paraphrased and simplified; confirm the sense (born among rakshasas, but not of their nature; left Ravana because of wrongdoing).
Lakshmana's vow (dharmātmā satyasandhaś ca rāmo dāśarathir yadi / pauruṣe cāpratidvandvas tadainaṃ jahi rāvaṇim): paraphrased in English; confirm the verse.
Suparshva's words to Ravana: paraphrased; confirm.
Indrajit's death kept unspecific (Valmiki: the arrow severs his head).
